common_name: São Tomé Highland Mist-Forest Fly (tan Enhancer Loss Yellow Abdomen)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila santomea (2.3 µm, detail scale)

specimen.license_note: Project species-gallery fallback. Wikimedia Commons had no still image (only PLOS ONE supplementary courtship videos). iNaturalist returned no taxon photo on 2026-10-27.
specimen.what_it_is: Sepia spiral-wave rendering with a drawn 100 µm scale bar and a caption. Not a micrograph that resolves 2.3 µm cuticle foci.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)

parameters.note: Not copied from the 102 µm santomea primordium slot (alpha_scale 1.555) or from the pseudoobscura/sechellia primordium slots.

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 derives the critical wavenumber from the linearized reaction-diffusion system.
Schnakenberg 1979 gives the two-species kinetics used here.
Jeong et al. 2008 Cell show that D. santomea lost abdominal expression of tan by cis-regulatory change, producing a yellow abdomen relative to D. yakuba.
Lachaise et al. 2000 described D. santomea from São Tomé.
Llopart et al. 2002 mapped the pigmentation difference between D. yakuba and D. santomea.
reconstructed_in_script: Assignment of the locked Jacobian to λ_c = 2.326 µm by choice of the spatial unit ξ.
Reading tan-enhancer loss as a reduced reaction-rate multiplier γ, so santomea is longer-wavelength than chronoseries neighbors pseudoobscura (1.840 µm) and sechellia (2.050 µm) at this same tier.
Numerical growth rates of eigenvector-initialized modes, equal-diffusion ablation, and the gallery scale-bar measurement.
does_not_claim: That Jeong, Llopart, or Lachaise measured a 2.3 µm Turing wavelength.
That abdominal pigmentation is known to be a Schnakenberg pattern.
That D. pseudoobscura is the ancestor of D. santomea. It is the chronoseries predecessor. The sister species is D. yakuba.
That the gallery spiral's arm spacing equals 2.326 µm. The drawn bar is 100 µm.
